class.name: CameraShake3D
class.brief_description: Shakes the active 3D camera for a short time.
class.description: When [method shake] is called, the current [Camera3D] of the viewport is rotated (pitch, yaw and roll) and slightly moved with smooth noise for [member duration] seconds. The shake is applied through [method Camera3D.add_shake_offset], an additive view offset, so it works with any player controller and combines with the game's own camera motion (head bob, recoil) instead of overwriting it. The intensity is [member strength] multiplied by the distance falloff: full strength within [member inner_radius], fading to zero at [member radius]. It decays smoothly over the duration. If no camera is current yet when [method shake] is called (for example an effect with autoplay starting together with the level), the shake waits up to half a second for one. As a child of a [ParticleEffect3D], it fires automatically at its start time (see [method ParticleEffect3D.set_emitter_delay]).

method.name: is_shaking
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the camera is being shaken.

method.name: shake
method.description: Starts shaking the current camera. A new shake on the same camera keeps the stronger of the two.

method.name: stop
method.description: Stops shaking and removes this node's offset from the camera.

members.member: Length of the shake in seconds.
Speed of the shake noise in Hz. Low values sway, high values rattle.
Distance from this node within which the camera shakes at full [member strength].
Maximum sideways and vertical camera movement in meters at full intensity.
Maximum camera rotation in degrees at full intensity: pitch (X), yaw (Y) and roll (Z).
Distance at which the shake fades out completely. [code]0[/code] shakes at full strength at any distance.
Intensity of the shake from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code] (values above [code]1[/code] exaggerate it). It scales [member max_rotation_degrees] and [member max_offset].

signal.name: shake_started
signal.description: Emitted when a shake starts, with the intensity after distance falloff. Connect it to drive extra game feedback such as controller rumble.
